slides.0.title: Roussillon VDN
slides.0.subtitle: Banyuls, Maury, Rivesaltes and Muscat de Rivesaltes
slides.1.title: What is a VDN
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Mutage
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Adding 5–10% grape spirit (min. 95% abv) mid-fermentation stops it and keeps the sugar (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Five AOPs
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Banyuls, Banyuls Grand Cru, Maury, Rivesaltes and Muscat de Rivesaltes (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Three ageing routes
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Broadly, reductive ageing that keeps fresh fruit versus oxidative, sun- or air-exposed ageing that builds rancio (a style generalisation)
slides.1.content: A VDN's style is really decided by how it is aged.
slides.2.title: Banyuls
slides.2.highlights.0.title: 1936 and 1962
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Banyuls in 1936; the infobox gives 1962 for Banyuls Grand Cru (Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Grenache share
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Grenache Noir at least 50%; Grand Cru at least 75% and at least 30 months' ageing (Wikipedia, French Entrée and Wine With Seth agree)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Terraces
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Vines grow on terraces on the slopes of the Catalan Pyrenees; some wines age outdoors in glass bottles in the sun and maderise
slides.2.content: Banyuls Grand Cru's two numbers (75%, 30 months) are the most asked.
slides.3.title: Maury
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The INAO recognised Maury as an AOC in 1936 (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Grenache at least 75%
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The rule is now at least 75% Grenache Noir (50% at creation); yield capped at 30 hL/ha; five communes: Maury, Saint-Paul-de-Fenouillet, Lesquerde, Tautavel and Rasiguères
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Rancio and bonbonnes
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Ageing often starts in 25-litre glass bonbonnes, with summer sun producing rancio; recent "vintage" Maurys are bottled early to keep fruit (Wikipedia)
slides.3.content: Maury and Banyuls both centre on Grenache but differ in soil and style.
slides.4.title: Rivesaltes and Muscat de Rivesaltes
slides.4.highlights.0.title: 1936 and 1972
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Rivesaltes AOC was created in 1936 and in 1972 combined several smaller designations (Wikipedia)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Four styles
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Ambré: at least 2 years oxidative ageing; Tuilé: red, at least 50% Grenache Noir, 2 years oxidative; Grenat: at least 12 months oxidative including 3 in bottle; Hors d'âge: ambré or tuilé aged 5 years
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Muscat de Rivesaltes
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Made only from Muscat varieties (French Entrée); Rivesaltes itself rests on Grenache (including Blanc and Gris), Macabeu and Malvoisie, with Muscat only an accessory under 20% (Wikipedia)
slides.4.content: Sources differ slightly on Rivesaltes ageing totals, so only the style definitions are used.
